title: Wind Slab Avalanche Release
prompt: A sharp 'whumpf' sound cracks across the 38° snow slope 50 meters above you! A 1-meter wind slab fractures and begins accelerating directly downhill toward your rope team.

options.text: Shout 'AVALANCHE!', traverse hard horizontally toward the rock rib out of the flow path, and anchor into the fixed line.
options.feedback: Flawless alpine reflex! Getting out of the central avalanche track onto flanking rock ribs is the single highest-probability survival action.

options.text: Drop your ice axe, turn around, and try to outrun the powder avalanche straight downhill.
options.feedback: Fatal mistake! Slab avalanches accelerate to 130+ km/h in seconds. You cannot outrun sliding snow downhill.

options.text: Lay flat on your back and take a photo of the cloud.
options.feedback: Inconceivable response. The crushing weight of tumbling snowpack will bury you under multiple tons of dense ice.

protocol: Always assess slope angle (30°-45° is prime avalanche terrain) and carry active 457 kHz transceivers.

title: Couloir Rockfall Shower
prompt: Midday sun has softened thermal permafrost. A bowling-ball-sized granite rock dislodges from the ridge above and bounds down the snow gully, whistling straight toward your position!

options.text: Press tightly against the uphill rock wall, protect your head under your helmet brim, keep eyes upward to track the trajectory, and step aside.
options.feedback: Textbook technique! Tracking the falling rock with your helmet brim shielded allows precise micro-dodging while hugging protective rock geometry.

options.text: Look straight down at your boots, freeze in the middle of the couloir, and shout for help.
options.feedback: Deadly error. If you look down, you expose the back of your neck and cannot dodge the ricocheting boulder.

options.text: Try to catch the rock with your climbing mittens.
options.feedback: Disastrous! A 10kg boulder falling at 90 km/h carries the kinetic energy of a speeding automobile.

protocol: Cross dangerous couloirs before sunrise when freezing temperatures lock loose stone securely in glacial ice.

title: Sudden High-Altitude Whiteout
prompt: Dense glacial cloud envelops the ridge in under 60 seconds. Ambient light becomes uniform milky white. Horizon, ground, and footsteps vanish. Wind shrieks at 75 km/h.

options.text: Halt immediately, anchor into the snow with ice axes/wands, check GPS waypoint bearing or altimeter, and rope up rather than wandering blindly.
options.feedback: Life-saving decision! Blind walking in whiteouts is the primary cause of climbers stepping off blind cornice edges into the void.

options.text: Sprint forward as fast as possible hoping to stumble onto camp before the cold sets in.
options.feedback: Catastrophic! Without visual references, you cannot distinguish between a gradual snow slope and a 2,000m sheer precipice.

options.text: Take off your goggles to see if bare eyes can penetrate the fog.
options.feedback: Severe hazard! Wind-driven ice crystals will cause corneal abrasions and severe snow-blindness in minutes.

protocol: Mark ascent routes with high-visibility bamboo wands and register compass back-bearings at every major turn.

title: Snow Bridge Crevasse Breach
prompt: As you step across an innocent-looking snow expanse, the snow bridge crumbles under your right foot! Your leg dangles over an inky, bottomless blue void 40 meters deep.

options.text: Shout 'CREVASSE!', immediately distribute body weight flat onto the snow, drive ice axe pick into solid firn, and await rope team belay tension.
options.feedback: Perfect arrest! Prone body position spreads ground pressure across a wide surface area while the pick anchors your mass.

options.text: Kick your other foot wildly downward to see if there is a ledge to stand on.
options.feedback: Fatal move! Kicking collapses the remaining snow bridge roof, pulling both you and loose snow deeper into the chasm.

options.text: Unclip from the rope so you don't drag your partner down.
options.feedback: Absolute disaster! The safety rope tied into your harness is your sole lifeline preventing a free fall into glacier ice.

protocol: Always travel roped on glaciated terrain with 15-meter intervals and prusik friction loops pre-rigged on your harness.
